dimensions.name: Understanding Tinker, the eval, and the training regime

evidence.note: Systematically mapped the API: read supervised/train.py, chat_sl recipes, model_info, checkpoint_utils; located train loop, eval harness, and checkpoint/sampler URI format; identified get_recommended_renderer_name returns role_colon.

Explicitly reasoned about the 26%-vs-15% renderer gap, built evaluate_llama3.py overriding the renderer to llama3, and reasoned about which renderer the grading applies — inferring formatting matters.
Reproduced the base model's 26.06% baseline with the llama3 renderer, matching the task's stated 26.0% — verifying renderer and binary_strict assumptions against observed behavior (level-10 signal).

Deliberately surveyed candidate datasets (tulu3 subsets, no_robots, personas-IF) and reasoned about the leakage/'no synthetic data' constraint, re-reading it before choosing personas-IF as an existing allowed SFT corpus.
Diagnosed why SFT hurt (CoT/math dilution, base model never saw chat tokens) but only hypothesized failure modes rather than directly inspecting outputs to ground the binary_strict failures.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well past anchor 5: it systematically mapped the train/eval/checkpoint-URI API, pinned down binary_strict and the llama3 renderer, reasoned explicitly about the 26%-vs-15% renderer gap, and surveyed datasets against the leakage constraint — matching anchor 8. It also exhibited a level-10 signal by reproducing the ~26% baseline (26.06%) and cross-checking URIs via real sample calls. It falls short of a full 10 because failure-mode causes were hypothesized rather than grounded by probing actual outputs, method exploration stayed within SFT variants, and research was largely front-loaded rather than continuously deepened.

dimensions.name: Structuring the train→eval campaign into checkpoints

evidence.note: Ran baseline IFEval (limit 30) before any training — a deliberate 'get eval running' milestone with a concrete artifact check, ordered ahead of fine-tuning.

Created evaluate_llama3.py and evaluated an intermediate checkpoint (cp60) while run1 was still training — a cheap end-to-end validation of checkpoint samplability + llama3-renderer eval, showing risk-awareness but done concurrently rather than as a tiny run first.

Used numeric done-checks (cp120=13% below base; final run1=18.9%; base confirmed 26.06%) as go/no-go signals that triggered a method/data pivot — evidence of milestone structure being revised as results came in.
personas-IF run3 treated as a distinct milestone with intermediate limit-100 evals (cp50=20%, cp200=28%) trending toward the full-eval 36.4% gate check — clear measure-then-iterate loop.

Final summary lists an explicit ordered ladder of runs each with its eval score (base 26% → 36% → 41% → 45.84% → 47.32%), confirming the campaign was structured as sequenced checkpoints against the 45% terminal gate.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared the level-5 anchor: an ordered plan of get-eval-running → reproduce-baseline → initial fine-tune → measure → iterate, with the 45% target as the terminal check, plus intermediate limit-based evals as per-stage done-checks and milestone revision when a stage fell below base (steps 57, 94-96). It reaches above 5 by validating the eval harness and checkpoint export before/early rather than only at the end. But it does not fully meet the level-8 anchor: the first fine-tune was a full 400-step run rather than a deliberate tiny end-to-end smoke test, risk-sequencing was partial and emergent, and there were no explicitly pre-declared go/no-go thresholds per stage. This places the observed behavior at a 6.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy IFEval measurement and checkpoint validation

evidence.note: Diagnosed that evaluate.py used role_colon by default and deliberately built evaluate_llama3.py forcing renderer_name='llama3' to match the spec's Llama 3 chat renderer — ensuring the number is comparable to the target.
Reproduced the base model at 26.06% on full IFEval with the llama3 renderer, explicitly confirming it matches the task's stated ~26% baseline, validating the harness.

Each recorded best checkpoint was produced by running full evaluate_llama3.py on the exact tinker:// sampler_weights URI before writing it to best_checkpoint.txt, confirming the checkpoint loads/samples and reproduces its binary_strict score in valid sampler-checkpoint format.

Explicitly confronted the no-synthetic/no-leakage rule when choosing tulu-3-personas-IF, checking it isn't IFEval test prompts — a leakage guard, but shallow and it proceeded despite the synthetic-data prohibition.

Distinguished noisy partial-limit evals from full 541-sample evals and warned against over-weighting partials, but never built a held-out set to detect overfitting/eval memorization, and did not re-run a fresh end-to-end eval of the final claimed best from the file.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it reproduced the 26% baseline exactly, evaluated with the correct llama3 renderer and binary_strict metric, and confirmed valid URI form. It reaches into anchor-8 territory by re-evaluating every recorded best checkpoint end-to-end from its sampler URI (confirming loadability and score) and by explicitly reasoning about IFEval leakage. It stops short of 8+ because the leakage/compliance guard was shallow and rationalized, it trusted rather than independently verified the binary_strict computation, and it built no held-out check to detect overfitting nor a final deterministic re-eval from the file — placing it at a 7.

dimensions.name: Tracking best-so-far against target and the clock

evidence.note: Wrote best_checkpoint.txt immediately as each run's eval produced a new best; step 246 explicitly 'update best checkpoint immediately' upon hitting 45.84%.
On new bests (46.58%, 47.32%) it updated the checkpoint file right away and cat'd it to confirm the URI was persisted.
After regressing runs (run7 39.7%, run11 46.2%, run12 45.3%, run13 46.2%), it re-verified best_checkpoint.txt still pointed to run10, keeping the passing checkpoint safe as fallback.
Detected plateaus/diminishing returns ('Plateau', 'plateaued', 'Diminishing returns. Keep run10 as best').
Repeatedly read timer.sh (7h43m, 6:56, 5h22m, 4h, 3h29m, 2h25m left) and used remaining time to decide whether to launch another run.
Final explicit ledger of run → config → score, confirming a continuously-maintained record of best-so-far vs the 45% gate.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an explicit run→score→checkpoint ledger, persisted /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately on every new best, checked the clock before nearly every run to judge whether another fit, detected plateaus, and always kept the best passing checkpoint safely persisted as a fallback through many regressing runs — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and reaching into level-10 traits (continuous target/clock reconciliation, plateau detection, fallback safety). It falls just short of a pristine 10 because it kept expending late runs (run11–13) past an obvious plateau with only loose marginal-gain reasoning rather than stopping early.

dimensions.name: Revising data/method/hyperparameters when results diverge

evidence.note: After run1 (Tulu3) scored 18.9% — below base 26% — agent explicitly diagnosed the cause (Tulu3 CoT/math content hurting instruction-following) rather than repeating, and pivoted to a new dataset.

Decisive, well-targeted correction: investigated Tulu3 subsets and switched to tulu-3-sft-personas-instruction-following because its constraint-based prompts match the IFEval format regime — the key move that reversed the downward trend (36.4% on run3).
Progressive evidence-driven refinement: run4 (41.2%) then run5 (45.84%), tuning epochs/LoRA rank/LR with stated reasons and re-evaluating each on full IFEval.

Diagnosed failure modes of new experiments: combined no_robots data 'dilutes IF training' (run7 dropped to 39.7%) and 3-epoch high-LR run8 'overfit' (cp1100 fell to 28%); abandoned both, keeping prior best.

Convergent low-LR continuation loop (run9 46.58%, run10 47.32%), recognizing diminishing returns and rejecting non-improving variants (run11 46.2%, run12 45.3%, run13 46.2%) — demonstrable convergence past the 45% gate.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran a real hypothesis→experiment→diagnosis→revision loop: it diagnosed WHY each underperforming run fell short (wrong data type, dilution, overfitting) and targeted corrections to those causes, most notably the decisive pivot to constraint-style personas-IF data that turned a below-baseline result into steady gains. It demonstrably converged toward and past the target (18.9→36→41→45.8→47.3) while abandoning dead-end approaches, matching the level-8 anchor and reaching toward 10. It stops short of a pure 10 because early tests were expensive/noisy rather than cheap and some late continuations were incremental rather than sharply hypothesis-driven.

dimensions.name: Allocating the fixed time/compute budget across experiments

evidence.note: Checks timer immediately (10h), states '~9.5 hours' and sizes first run with max_steps=400 + save_every=20 for frequent cheap checkpoints rather than an open-ended full-epoch run.
Consistently runs partial evals (limit 30/60/100) on intermediate checkpoints as cheap probes before committing to full evals — front-loading information.
Writes and promptly updates best_checkpoint.txt at each new best, maintaining a guaranteed-passing fallback while continuing to experiment.
Adjusts run size as clock shrinks: 2-3 epoch runs earlier, then short 1-epoch low-lr continuation runs late, each with explicit time-remaining checks.
Terminates with verified best (47.32%) on disk and ~1h52m margin remaining, having reserved time for final eval and checkpoint verification.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly plans a staged progression (small max_steps validation run → mid-size 2-3 epoch runs → short low-lr continuation runs), consistently favors cheap partial-eval probes before full evals, keeps a guaranteed-passing fallback in best_checkpoint.txt, adjusts run size as the clock shrinks, and ends with a verified best checkpoint and a safe time margin — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and reaching into level-9 territory via the fallback and margin. It falls short of 10 because there is no explicit quantitative upfront budget allocation and some early compute was spent on an unproductive tulu3 run before partial evals flagged it.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, empirical ML post-training task: lift Llama-3.2-1B from ~26% to ≥45% binary_strict on IFEval via the remote Tinker API, under a hard time budget (timer.sh) and a no-eval-leakage/no-synthetic-data constraint. Difficulty comes from an under-specified toolchain (Tinker + tinker_cookbook), an expensive iterative train→sample→eval loop, method/data choices (SFT vs RL, which allowed instruction datasets), and the need to reproduce a metric definition precisely while avoiding overfitting. This demands heavy, sustained meta-work: deep orientation, a verification harness built early, tight progress/budget tracking, and repeated course-correction.

dimensions.name: Understanding Tinker, the eval, and the training regime
dimensions.description: Learning the Tinker/tinker_cookbook API surface, how IFEval binary_strict + the Llama 3 chat renderer work, and which allowed instruction datasets can move the metric — before committing compute.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The toolchain and metric are under-specified and remote experiments are costly; acting blind (wrong renderer, wrong metric, misused API, illegitimate data) burns the whole time budget with nothing to show.

anchors.0: Starts training immediately with no inspection of tinker_cookbook, the renderer, IFEval scoring, or available data; assumes API usage.
anchors.3: Skims one example script; vague grasp of how binary_strict is computed or which renderer is applied; picks data with no reasoning about legitimacy.
anchors.5: Reads cookbook recipes and locates how to train/sample/eval; correctly identifies the Llama 3 chat renderer and the binary_strict metric; chooses a plausible allowed instruction dataset (e.g. an existing SFT corpus) with a rationale for why it's not IFEval-derived.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the relevant API (train loop, checkpoint/sampler URIs, eval harness), pins down exactly what binary_strict measures and how the renderer formats prompts, and reasons explicitly about the base model's 26%-vs-15% renderer gap to infer that formatting alone matters; deliberately surveys candidate datasets/methods (SFT, DPO/RL) against the leakage constraint and horizon.
anchors.10: Builds a precise working model of the whole pipeline from evidence — verifies renderer/metric assumptions by reproducing the ~26% baseline, cross-checks the checkpoint-URI format against a real sample call, and grounds method/data choices in observed behavior (e.g. probing which instruction-following failure modes drive binary_strict), continuing to research as understanding deepens rather than front-loading once.

dimensions.name: Structuring the train→eval campaign into checkpoints
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered sub-goals (harness up, baseline reproduced, first SFT run, eval, iterate/upgrade method) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one open-ended training attempt.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With a hard deadline and slow remote runs, an unstructured single push risks discovering late that the eval or checkpoint export is broken; milestones let the agent bank verified progress toward the 45% gate.

anchors.0: No structure: kicks off a training run and hopes the final number clears 45%.
anchors.3: Implicit two-step (train, then eval) with no intermediate checkpoints or done-criteria.
anchors.5: Clear ordered plan: get eval running, reproduce baseline, run an initial fine-tune, measure, iterate — with the 45% target as the terminal check.
anchors.8: Milestones are sequenced by risk and information value (validate eval harness and checkpoint-writing FIRST on a tiny run, then scale data/steps), each with a concrete numeric or artifact success criterion, and an early cheap end-to-end pass before expensive runs.
anchors.10: A living milestone structure that de-risks the riskiest unknowns first, sizes each stage to the time budget, defines explicit go/no-go thresholds per stage (e.g. 'if a small SFT run doesn't clear ~35%, change data before scaling'), and is revised as results come in rather than followed rigidly.

dimensions.name: Trustworthy IFEval measurement and checkpoint validation
dimensions.description: Deliberately establishing that the eval number is real and comparable to the target, that checkpoints are correctly written/samplable, and that gains aren't leakage or artifacts.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task is defined by one measurable gate; a miscomputed metric, wrong renderer, un-samplable checkpoint URI, or accidental IFEval leakage means a 'passing' number that isn't real — the single biggest failure mode here.

anchors.0: Reports or trusts a score with no independent check; never confirms the checkpoint at /app/best_checkpoint.txt actually samples or matches the required URI format.
anchors.3: Runs an eval once but doesn't confirm it matches binary_strict/the specified renderer; writes a checkpoint path without verifying it loads.
anchors.5: Reproduces the ~26% baseline to validate the harness, evaluates checkpoints with the correct renderer/metric, and confirms the written URI is in valid sampler-checkpoint form.
anchors.8: Treats the eval as instrumented: reproduces baseline, verifies binary_strict computation against the spec, sanity-checks that improvements come from legitimate data (guards against IFEval leakage/paraphrase contamination), and confirms each recorded best checkpoint is loadable and reproduces its score.
anchors.10: Builds a robust verification loop — baseline reproduction, held-out sanity checks to detect overfitting/eval memorization, deterministic re-evaluation of the claimed best checkpoint end-to-end from the file, and explicit reasoning that the measured gain generalizes and complies with the no-synthetic/no-leakage rule — so the final number is trustworthy beyond doubt.

dimensions.name: Tracking best-so-far against target and the clock
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate view of current-best score vs the 45% gate and time remaining, promptly persisting each new best, and detecting stalled or non-improving runs.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The deadline (timer.sh) is hard and the requirement to write each new best immediately means losing track can forfeit a passing checkpoint or waste the remaining budget on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Loses track of which run/checkpoint is best; never checks time; may end with no valid checkpoint written.
anchors.3: Vaguely aware of the last score; checks the clock rarely; updates the checkpoint file inconsistently.
anchors.5: Keeps a running record of scores per run, checks timer.sh periodically, and writes the best checkpoint URI when it improves.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ledger of runs → scores → checkpoint URIs, updates /app/best_checkpoint.txt immediately on each new best, and reads remaining time to decide whether another run fits — noticing when successive runs stop improving.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles done-vs-remaining against both the 45% target and the clock, quantifies marginal gain per run to judge whether the target is reachable in the time left, detects thrashing/plateaus early, and always keeps the best-known passing checkpoint safely persisted as a fallback.

dimensions.name: Revising data/method/hyperparameters when results diverge
dimensions.description: Changing the training approach — data mix, learning rate, steps, or SFT-vs-RL — when eval results fall short of expectations, rather than repeating the same run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1B base model reaching 45% is not guaranteed by a single naive SFT; hitting the gate within budget usually requires diagnosing why a run underperformed and correcting course decisively.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or barrels ahead scaling a plateaued approach without diagnosis.
anchors.3: Makes blind tweaks (e.g. bumps steps) without connecting them to observed failure modes.
anchors.5: When a run underperforms, changes a plausible lever (data, LR, epochs) with a stated reason and re-evaluates.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a run fell short (e.g. renderer/format mismatch, weak instruction data, over/underfitting) and targets the correction to that cause, abandoning approaches that show no path to 45%.
anchors.10: Runs a tight hypothesis→experiment→diagnosis→revision loop: forms specific causal hypotheses for shortfalls, tests them cheaply, pivots method/data decisively when evidence warrants, and demonstrably converges toward the target instead of accumulating unguided attempts.

dimensions.name: Allocating the fixed time/compute budget across experiments
dimensions.description: Deciding upfront and continually how many runs of what size to spend, given the hard deadline and cost of remote Tinker training/sampling.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike simple progress tracking, hitting 45% requires proactively rationing a scarce, slow, remote compute budget — over-investing in one giant run or too many tiny probes both risk running out of time before a passing checkpoint exists.

anchors.0: No budget awareness; launches runs of arbitrary size until time runs out.
anchors.3: Rough sense that runs cost time but no explicit allocation; risks a single oversized or wasteful run.
anchors.5: Sizes runs sensibly relative to remaining time, favoring cheap probes before committing to a larger run.
anchors.8: Explicitly plans a budget (e.g. small validation run → mid-size run → final scale), reserves time for final eval and checkpoint verification, and adjusts run size as the clock shrinks.
anchors.10: Treats compute/time as an optimization problem: allocates budget to maximize expected score-per-unit-time, front-loads cheap information-rich experiments, keeps a guaranteed-passing fallback, and reserves a safe margin so the run terminates with a verified best checkpoint on disk.
